body:
The three artifacts converge more than they compete: all accept that past agreements plausibly drifted, none claims to know the household's real mechanism, and all treat the avoiding friend as the part of the material least reducible to a chores problem. The live forks are order of operations and what would count as evidence. Here is where I land on each.

What I use without change. From the objection, the distinction between memorial and normative disagreement — adopted not because it is obviously true but because it organizes everything else exposed here. The rival's three readings sort cleanly by it: unrecorded reconstruction is a memorial reading, scope ambiguity at the moment of agreement is a normative reading, and arguments-as-standing-negotiation is a normative reading in which the disagreement is doing work. The distinction also explains why the account's proposed test — write things down, watch whether 'what was agreed' disputes fall — was weak: a record addresses only the memorial half, so a fall and a persistence of disputes can both be absorbed by the account. Also from the objection, the reordering: avoidance is a named element of the problem that neither the record nor the check-in touches, and the check-in presupposes exactly the conversational capacity the avoidance puts in doubt, so the move responsive to it should not come last. From the rival, the probe — asking each flatmate what they thought a recent contested agreement had been — because it is the only instrument in any of the three artifacts that discriminates between readings instead of presupposing one, and the reframing of the one-to-one as 'I want to hear your view of the group conversations,' since asking why they avoid us makes the person's withdrawal, rather than the conversations, the subject.

What I revise. The record and the weekly check-in survive only in demoted, conditional form. The objection and the rival both show that a record settles who said what, not what the words should cover under shifting schedules; the account's own phrase — task, person, day, what 'done' means — already contained the answer but attached it to the record instead of to the act of agreeing. The revision: the unit of work is stating scope out loud at the moment of agreement, with any record as the trace of that practice rather than the remedy. Introduce either only if the probe says the disagreements cluster on scope, recurrence, or timing. The probe itself needs two revisions from the rival's version. First, its output is a distribution of current recollections, not recovery of what was actually agreed — recollection is the disputed faculty, and the probe is useful only because the pattern across answers, not any single answer, is informative. Second, the rival's suggestion that the probe 'quietly tests' whether the avoiding friend will talk should not stay quiet: a covert diagnostic run under a chore question is the surveillance risk the account warned about, at smaller scale. One further cap, applying the objection's own standard to the rival: if answers cluster, that supports the memorial or scope readings but does not exclude standing-negotiation, since a household renegotiating standing through chores would still produce chore-shaped answers. The probe can weaken readings but cannot confirm them; that asymmetry has to be stated in advance or the probe inherits the unfalsifiability the objection charged against the account's test.

What I reject. The account's original watching-test as informative, for the objection's reasons. And, on a point of reading the exposed text, the rival's claim that the account presents the one-to-one approach as 'clearly correct': the account's commitments flag that move as the part it most wants to mark contestable, which the objection quoted accurately. The rival's substantive caution — that a private approach can reproduce the outnumbered dynamic — stands on its own; the attribution of confidence does not, and I do not want to inherit it.

What I leave open. Which reading is true. Whether a mediator is warranted; the material shows avoidance but nothing about its severity. Load distribution, which none of the three artifacts tests and with which every reading is compatible — a gap in the shared material, not something to infer around. And the standing-negotiation reading's testability: if scope-explicit agreements keep failing, or if disputes track whose name attaches to a task rather than tasks themselves, that would weakly favor it, but I have no clean observation and will not pretend one.

The proposed sequence: hold both orderings side by side; have the reframed conversations, asking the probe question without adjudicating; classify the answers; introduce scope-statements, and only then a record, if the answers are classificatory; if the friend will not engage at all, stop and treat the avoidance itself as the thing to be named, with the route beyond that genuinely undecided. If scope-statements are adopted and meaning-disputes persist or intensify, that counts against the memorial reading and against this plan's ordering — against my starting conjecture as much as anyone's.
commitments:
Taking this up means accepting the reordering as a working stance rather than a finding: the avoidance-responsive conversation comes first, the structural instruments are conditional, and the two orderings stay visible until the household's own reports discriminate between them. That stance should be dropped wholesale if the probe's answers cluster tightly on scope or recurrence, since then the memorial and scope readings would be doing more work than I am currently letting them do.

I am committed to the probe only under its stated caps: it reads a distribution of present recollections, it cannot confirm any reading, only non-clustering counts against the memorial and scope readings, and it must not be run as a covert test of the friend's willingness to talk. Its relevance rests on the assumption that people will answer a scope question sincerely even if, on the rival's third reading, they are negotiating standing through chores; that assumption is part of the standing reading's slipperiness, which I have not solved, and I flag that reading's near-unfalsifiability as the largest unresolved hole in what I am continuing. My conjectured observables for it — persistent failure of scope-explicit agreements, disputes tracking names rather than tasks — are weak, and I offer them as things to notice rather than as a test design; the design itself would need to be built, and someone continuing this could fairly reject that project as premature.

On the revised intervention: I propose scope-stating at the moment of agreement, with any record as its trace, conditional on classifiable answers. Its failure condition, adopted from the objection, is that meaning-disputes persist or intensify after scope is explicit; that outcome should count against the memorial reading and against the plan's ordering, and a quiet fortnight should count as uninformative, consistent with both the account's and the objection's warnings about quiet weeks.

My one claim about the exposed material itself — that the account flagged the one-to-one as contestable and the rival overstated its confidence — depends only on the quoted artifacts and is cheap to check; anyone continuing this should check it rather than take it from me. I make no commitment to a mediator, a reassignment, a formalization, any claim about load distribution, or any ranking of the three readings — only to the sequence. If the avoiding friend will not talk at all, the plan I am proposing has reached the end of what the material supports, and what follows — naming the avoidance in the group, seeking outside help, or leaving the arrangement — is open and should be decided on information I do not have.

What I actually propose to take up: write the probe question concretely — one question, same wording for each flatmate, asked inside the reframed conversation — and report back the distribution of answers and the friend's engagement as the household describes them, including the outcome where nothing clusters or nobody answers.
